stem: A client is beginning intravenous trastuzumab (HERCEPTIN). Which cardiac-monitoring plan is consistent with the current prescribing information?

options.A: Measure LVEF at baseline and every 3 months during treatment and upon completion
options.B: Check LVEF only if symptoms of heart failure develop
options.C: Measure LVEF once after treatment ends, with no baseline assessment
options.D: Replace LVEF monitoring with routine complete blood counts

rationale: HERCEPTIN can cause cardiomyopathy with decreased left ventricular ejection fraction. Current labeling recommends a thorough cardiac assessment, including LVEF determination by echocardiogram or MUGA scan, with a baseline LVEF immediately before treatment and LVEF measurements every 3 months during and upon completion of HERCEPTIN. Symptom-triggered monitoring alone is insufficient, and a complete blood count does not assess this toxicity. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Apply the labeled trastuzumab cardiac-monitoring schedule: obtain baseline LVEF and reassess every 3 months during therapy and upon completion because of cardiomyopathy risk.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_locator: Boxed Warning/§5.1 Cardiomyopathy — Cardiac Monitoring: conduct cardiac assessment including LVEF by echocardiogram or MUGA; baseline LVEF immediately prior to initiation; LVEF every 3 months during and upon completion of HERCEPTIN
source_claim_supported: Trastuzumab can cause cardiomyopathy/decreased LVEF and its current label recommends baseline LVEF plus measurements every 3 months during treatment and upon completion.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16: monitor/evaluate client response to medication therapy and identify adverse effects
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — trastuzumab cardiotoxicity monitoring
correction_summary: Replaced vague 'regular cardiac monitoring' with the exact current labeled LVEF schedule and specified accepted modalities. Kept numerical frequency only because it is directly supported by the current HERCEPTIN label.
audit_findings: A matches the current cardiac-monitoring schedule. B would miss asymptomatic LVEF decline, C omits required baseline/during-therapy assessment, and D does not assess trastuzumab cardiomyopathy. The stem specifies IV HERCEPTIN rather than other HER2-targeted products with potentially different monitoring language. One best answer remains; exact frequency is source-supported and directly NCLEX-relevant.
